catalog_quote: [p.152, sec. 11 TONE TYPOLOGY] Tone is a prominent feature of all Lakes Plain languages and therefore was most likely a feature of some of the protolanguages as well. This fact further distances Lakes Plain languages from the Trans New Guinea Phylum. All the modem languages have at least high and low tone. Duvle and Sikaritai have only these tones with Martin ( 1 99 1) analysing the Sikaritai system as pitch-accent. The remainder of the languages also have combinations of high and low (or contours); Obokuitai has a fall (Jenison 199 1), Doutai (McAllister 1 99 1), Edopi (Kim 1 995) and all the western Tariku languages have a fall and a rise (Clouse n.d. !). [p.160, Appendix 3] Although tonal contrast is found in virtually all of the Lakes Plain languages, it will not be shown in the word list transcriptions. new_statements.rule_in_words: All Lakes Plain languages, Biritai included, are tonal (at least H vs L); stress has not been found contrastive in any Lakes Plain language. This is a family-wide remark in a comparative paper; no statement of where stress falls in Biritai (or any placement rule) exists in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the remark is hedged ('to date') and family-level. Sikaritai (a sister East Tariku language) is noted as analysed as pitch accent by Martin 1991; Obokuitai has H, L and a fall (Jenison 1991) -- neither is Biritai.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement scope is the whole Lakes Plain family (20 languages in Clouse's word lists), not Biritai specifically; Biritai evidence is a survey wordlist Clouse elicited himself in Biri village, October 1992. Word-level transcription conventions only; no phrase-level discussion.
new_statements.first_reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.identity_note: Clouse 1997's remark is family-wide (all Lakes Plain languages), not a Biritai-specific description; his Biritai data are a survey wordlist from Biri village (Oct 1992). Glottolog 5.1's descriptive ref Prost 1973 'Les langues de l'Atakora III: Le Biɛri' is a misattribution (a Gur language of Benin, cf. bial1246 Biali), not Biritai. Nearest described relatives Obokuitai (obok1239) and Sikaritai (sika1262) have SIL phonologies (Workpapers vol. 9, 1991) but are distinct languages.
